Synopsis:
    Mongolia is experiencing fuel shortages and sharp price increases (from ~$1/L to $1.5–2/L) as a direct spillover from Russia's domestic fuel crunch, itself driven by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries and elevated seasonal demand. Despite an exemption from Russia's export ban under bilateral agreements, Russian motor fuel exports to Mongolia declined month-on-month in July. Diesel volumes for Jan–Jul rose 7% YoY, but gasoline and jet fuel flows are under strain. The article was reported on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, where Putin and Mongolia's PM affirmed a deepened strategic partnership.
